messages.subject: arrange() with lubridate objects fail

require(plyr)
require(lubridate)

tasks<-structure(list(SMC.PI = c(8893L, 8893L, 8893L, 8893L, 8893L, 8893L, 8893L, 8893L, 8893L, 8893L), SubProject = structure(c(1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L), .Label = "Ripening Physiology", class = "factor"),     SubSubProject = structure(c(1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L,     1L, 1L), .Label = "Fruit Color", class = "factor"), Workstream.ID = structure(c(1L,     1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 2L), .Label = c("1.2.1.04",     "1.2.1.06"), class = "factor"), Workstream.Name = structure(c(1L,     1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 2L), .Label = c("Pepper",     "Tomato"), class = "factor"), Process = structure(c(8L, 3L,     5L, 6L, 1L, 7L, 4L, 5L, 2L, 8L), .Label = c("Analytical",     "Candidate Gene", "Cultivation", "Data Analysis", "QTL Analysis",     "Sampling", "Sequencing", "Total"), class = "factor"), Owner = structure(c(4L,     6L, 3L, 2L, 5L, 1L, 4L, 3L, 4L, 4L), .Label = c("?", "BA",     "GPL", "Hurr", "Kende", "Nicolet"), class = "factor"), Location = structure(c(2L,     3L, 1L, 3L, 2L, 4L, 2L, 1L, 2L, 2L), .Label = c("FRSS", "GBJH",     "MAAG", "USRE"), class = "factor"), Cost = c(NA, NA, NA,     NA, NA, NA, NA, NA, NA, NA), DurationMonths = c(36L, 9L,     1L, 1L, 3L, 2L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 36L), Start = structure(c(1L,     3L, 4L, 5L, 6L, 6L, 7L, 8L, 9L, 2L), .Label = c("2011-01-01",     "2011-10-01", "2012-11-01", "2013-02-01", "2013-05-01", "2013-06-01",     "2013-09-01", "2013-10-01", "2013-11-01"), class = "factor"),     End = structure(c(8L, 3L, 1L, 2L, 4L, 3L, 5L, 6L, 7L, 9L), .Label = c("2013-03-01",     "2013-06-01", "2013-08-01", "2013-09-01", "2013-10-01", "2013-11-01",     "2013-12-01", "2014-01-01", "2014-10-01"), class = "factor")), .Names = c("SMC.PI", "SubProject", "SubSubProject", "Workstream.ID", "Workstream.Name", "Process", "Owner", "Location", "Cost", "DurationMonths", "Start", "End"), class = "data.frame", row.names = c(NA, -10L))

#make dates first
tasks$Start<-parse_date_time(tasks$Start, orders="Y-m-d")
tasks$End<-parse_date_time(tasks$End, orders="Y-m-d")

#sort task by start date
tasks<-ddply(tasks, .(Workstream.ID), function(x) arrange(x, Start))
#fails Error: Length of ordering vectors don't match data frame size

But if you reverse the order (sort then make dates) it works. Can arrange() not arrange dates? I've even tried as.numeric(Start) and that doesn't help. Also, I tried the development version of plyr.

On Fri, Dec 7, 2012 at 5:30 PM, Dennis Murphy <djm...@gmail.com> wrote:
Hi Brandon:

On Fri, Dec 7, 2012 at 1:56 AM, Brandon Hurr <brando...@gmail.com> wrote:
> Dennis,
>
> Thanks for the sanity check, but I still get the error even after updating.
> It could have something to do with the output of lubridate. I notice that
> the datatype of the time output from Lubridate is different than yours.
> POSIXlt not POSIXct. I'm not sure if that's the difference.

I think it is. POSIXlt is a list object of length 9. I seem to recall
several posts in the list archives where ggplot2 didn't behave as
expected unless the date objects were POSIXct. Here's a post from
Hadley in Dec. 2009:

----------------
        > Just for the sake of completeness: there are several date formats in
        > R, the ones I have had success with and that seem to be the most
        > official ones are POSIXct and POSIXlt. Lookup the help for those.
        >
        > See R News Volume 1/2, June 2001 for more info (even if it
is a bit dated).
           I'd recommend Date and POSIXct.  POSIXlt doesn't work with
data frames.

    Hadley

----------------
